This page makes none. It tells you who Mr. Jay is, what he is qualified to do, how he teaches, and what he will not promise, so you can decide whether this way of learning fits you. Who Mr. Jay is His full name is Nathaniel Jay Adams. Learners know him as Mr. Jay Adams, or thầy Jay. He is American and is based in Hanoi. He holds two roles. At Jurassic English he is Founder and Lead Coach. Jurassic English supports academic English, critical thinking and IELTS-style Speaking practice. Both roles come back to one question: what is actually holding this learner back, and how do we show it with evidence rather than impressions? Qualifications CELTA (Cambridge) , a Cambridge qualification for teaching English to adults, built around planning, teaching and receiving feedback on real lessons. Advanced TEFL Certificate, 120 hours , International TESOL TEFL Academy. iPGCE, in progress , University of Warwick. Google Certified Educator, Level 1 and Level 2. M.S. in Information Technology Management , 2017. CELTA and TEFL are the language-teaching foundation. The iPGCE is the wider pedagogy. The IT degree and Google certifications are why he builds AI speaking tools himself, and why he is plain about what those tools cannot do. How he teaches IELTS Speaking Find what is most likely holding the speaking band down. Not every error. The one that matters most. Show the evidence from your own answer. Which sentence, which moment, and why it weakens the answer. Pick one priority. Fixing five things at once usually means fixing none of them properly. Teach structure, not memorised answers. A structure works on a topic you have never seen. A model answer works only on its own question. Use your strengths to fix the weakness. Strong vocabulary can carry a short answer further. Fluent speech can be given a frame so it stays on point. Re-measure. Answer again, compare with last time, and check whether the priority has moved. Every session covers four things: evidence from the response, guided practice, an independent attempt and a practical follow-up. The evidence picks the priority, guided practice teaches the structure, the independent attempt is the re-measure, and the follow-up keeps practice going between lessons. h1: Your Speaking baseline, with a person
description: A 15–20 minute live IELTS-style Speaking mock test on Google Meet with a Jurassic English assessor: four criterion bands, an overall band and a written plan. For adults and learners under 18 when a parent or legal guardian books and consents. Not an official IELTS score.
text: Jurassic English ™ Menu Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing EN | VI Book the Live Baseline → JURASSIC ENGLISH · LIVE SPEAKING BASELINE Your Speaking baseline, with a person One live conversation, three parts, assessed against the four criteria in the public IELTS Speaking band descriptors. You leave with four criterion bands, an overall band and a plan built on your weakest criterion. Sessions with learners under 18 are never recorded. Book → Tiếng Việt 690.000₫ · one 15–20 minute live session A live session on Google Meet with your assessor Four criterion bands and an overall band A written plan built on your weakest criterion What it is How it works Set-up Recording & privacy Common mistakes After Book Practice assessment by Jurassic English, not an official IELTS score. Independent; not endorsed by IELTS, the British Council, IDP or Cambridge University Press & Assessment. What this session is One conversation in three parts, timed like the IELTS Speaking test and assessed live by your assessor, Nathaniel Jay Adams. Because the format and the clock are the same every time, your baseline can be compared with a re-test later. Mode Online Google Meet, camera on. Recording is optional and only with your consent. Form A or B Two parallel forms of equal difficulty. You sit one; the other is kept for your re-test. Result Four bands Plus an overall band and a written plan for what to work on next. How the assessment works The session, minute by minute Choose a stage to see what happens in it. Use the arrow keys to move between stages. 2 min Set-up 4–5 min Part 1 3–4 min Part 2 5–6 min Part 3 1–2 min Wrap-up Set-up · 2 min Greeting, identity check, the recording question and a microphone and camera test. The set-up is not assessed: it exists so that your first assessed answer is not your most nervous one. Part 1 · 4–5 min Five questions on one familiar topic, asked in order. Answer in two or three sentences: enough to show natural speech, never a memorised paragraph. Part 2 · 3–4 min A task card, one minute of preparation with written notes, then an uninterrupted long turn of one to two minutes, closed by two short follow-up questions. Part 3 · 5–6 min A two-way discussion of broader questions linked to your Part 2 theme: opinion, comparison, speculation. No factual knowledge is assessed. Wrap-up · 1–2 min Any recording is stopped and next steps are confirmed. Your four criterion bands are finalised after the session ends, never while you are still speaking. About 15–20 minutes in total. What your assessor listens for Four criteria, equally weighted. Choose one to open it. FC Fluency and Coherence LR Lexical Resource GRA Grammatical Range and Accuracy PR Pronunciation Fluency and Coherence Rate and pausing · cohesion Can you keep speaking at a comfortable rate, and do your ideas connect? Your assessor listens for pausing that reflects thinking rather than searching for words, and for linking language such as “because”, “although”, “what I mean is”, “the other thing is”. Lexical Resource Range · collocation How wide and how natural is your vocabulary? Precise words and natural pairings matter more than rare words: “heavy traffic”, not “strong traffic”. Paraphrasing well when a word escapes you also counts here. Grammatical Range and Accuracy Complexity · control Do you use a range of tenses and sentence structures, and control them? Occasional slips are normal. What holds a band down is frequent error in basic structures. Pronunciation Intelligibility · stress Can you be understood without effort from the listener? Individual sounds, word stress and sentence rhythm all count. Accent is never marked down; being understood is what is assessed. These four criteria are the ones in the public IELTS Speaking band descriptors. How your overall band is worked out Each criterion receives a whole band, and the four count equally. Your assessor averages them and rounds the result down to the nearest half band, so 5.25 becomes 5.0 and 5.75 becomes 5.5. IELTS publishes the equal weighting but not how this average is rounded, so we round down: your baseline never shows a higher band than your answers support. Example: FC 6 · LR 6 · GRA 5 · PR 6 → 23 ÷ 4 = 5.75 → overall 5.5. All four criterion bands are reported alongside the overall band; that detail is where the coaching starts. Try the arithmetic Move each criterion and watch the overall band change. Fluency and Coherence 6 Lexical Resource 6 Grammatical Range and Accuracy 5 Pronunciation 6 Overall band 5.5 23 ÷ 4 = 5.75 A demonstration of the arithmetic only. Your real bands come from the live session. The lower half of the scale (bands 1–5) Most people start their preparation somewhere on this part of the scale. It is a starting point, not a ceiling. 5 Modest user . Partial command; copes with overall meaning in most situations, though likely to make many mistakes. 4 Limited user . Basic competence limited to familiar situations; frequent problems in understanding and expression. 3 Extremely limited user . Conveys and understands only general meaning in very familiar situations; frequent breakdowns in communication. 2 Intermittent user . Great difficulty understanding spoken and written English. 1 Non-user . No ability to use the language beyond a few isolated words. Summary of the band scale published at ielts.org (“IELTS scoring in detail”). The scale is owned by the British Council, IDP IELTS and Cambridge University Press & Assessment. Half bands sit between these levels. For orientation: around band 7 speech is fluent and flexible; around band 6 it copes with most topics with some imprecision; around band 5 it manages familiar topics with noticeable hesitation. Before you start: your set-up Tick each item as you prepare it. Your ticks stay on this device only. Headphones with a microphone, to prevent echo A quiet room with the door closed Camera on, with the light in front of your face Photo ID within reach for the identity check (shown on camera, never copied or kept) Paper and a pen for your Part 2 notes Other applications closed, for a stable connection 0 of 6 ready If your connection drops, the clock is paused and the session resumes from the last complete question. Recording and privacy Optional Recording is optional and only with your consent; without it the session runs on live notes. Sessions with learners under 18 are never recorded. Asked twice You choose when you book, and you are asked again on camera before anything is recorded. You can say no at either point. What and why If you agree, only the assessed part is recorded, so each band can be checked against the descriptors and turned into specific feedback. Kept 30 days Your assessor deletes any recording within 30 days of your session. Your booking and bands are kept for 24 months for accounting. Under 18 A parent or guardian books the session and gives consent, and is asked to confirm it on camera at the start. No AI Nothing about this session is sent to an AI service, and no audio passes through this website. Google and SePay Your session is added to our Google Calendar with a Meet link (Google stores this outside Vietnam), and SePay tells us when your transfer arrives. The calendar event shows only your booking code, email and time. Full privacy notice → Mistakes that cost bands Open a card to see the fix. One-word answers Add the reason. “Yes, because…” shows you can extend an answer. Show the fix Memorised speeches Assessors notice them quickly, and they stop counting as your own language. Show the fix Freezing after an error Correct yourself once, then continue. Silence costs more than a wrong tense. Show the fix Advanced words used loosely A precise common word does better than an impressive wrong one. Show the fix Speaking too quickly Speed is not fluency. A clear rhythm helps; a rush that blurs words does not. Show the fix Never asking for repetition “Sorry, could you repeat that?” is allowed, costs nothing and sounds natural. Show the fix After your baseline I Your four bands Each criterion band, with what already works and where the ceiling sits. II Your target A realistic target band and the date you need it by: university, visa or a personal goal. III Your plan What to work on first, built around your weakest criterion, and a re-test on the parallel form when you are ready. title: Luyện IELTS Speaking online với AI: thi thử, band ước tính và phản hồi | Jurassic English
h1: Bạn không thể học thuộc kỳ thi IELTS.   Hãy học cách xây dựng câu trả lời.
description: Luyện IELTS Speaking online với AI bằng câu trả lời đánh máy. Xem bằng chứng từ chính bài làm, khoảng điểm ước tính và một việc cần luyện tiếp. Không đánh giá phát âm từ văn bản; không phải điểm IELTS chính thức.
text: Jurassic English ™ Menu Học viện Thiếu nhi (5–12 tuổi) 9–18 tuổi IELTS Writing Mới Thi thử Nói AI Học phí EN | VI Xem các gói lượt → LUYỆN IELTS SPEAKING CHO NGƯỜI LỚN Bạn không thể học thuộc kỳ thi IELTS. Hãy học cách xây dựng câu trả lời. Đánh máy câu trả lời Phần 1–3. Xem bằng chứng đằng sau ước tính luyện tập và một thay đổi quan trọng nhất cho lần tới. Bắt đầu bài luyện tập → Xem các gói lượt Khám phá buổi học 1 kèm 1 → Ước tính luyện tập bằng AI · Độc lập · Không phải điểm IELTS chính thức Những gì bạn dùng được ngay hôm nay Chế độ đánh máy: dùng được ngay. Đánh máy câu trả lời Phần 1–3 và nhận báo cáo trích dẫn chính lời bạn, kèm ước tính cho Độ trôi chảy & mạch lạc, Từ vựng và Ngữ pháp. Chế độ đánh máy không đánh giá phát âm. Chế độ nói: beta giới hạn. Trả lời bằng giọng nói hiện chỉ mở cho người được mời. Âm thanh mẫu. Câu trả lời mẫu trên trang AI Speaking là giọng đọc tổng hợp do AI tạo để minh họa, không phải bản ghi của học viên. Cần đủ bốn tiêu chí, kể cả phát âm? Buổi Đánh giá Nói trực tiếp 15–20 phút (690.000₫) là một buổi riêng qua Google Meet, do người thật chấm theo cả bốn tiêu chí. Đánh giá Nói trực tiếp → Ví dụ minh họa chế độ nói Chế độ nói đang ở beta giới hạn Khám phá phần phân tích 6.5 LUYỆN TẬP Tóm tắt phiên phân tích Bài Part 3 Chủ đề: sản phẩm thân thiện với môi trường Đã xác định ưu tiên Chọn một tiêu chí. Theo dõi bằng chứng. Thử bước luyện tiếp theo. Độ trôi chảy & mạch lạc 6.0 Từ vựng 6.5 Ngữ pháp 6.5 Phát âm 6.5 Vì sao có mức ước tính này? · Độ trôi chảy & mạch lạc Ý kiến → lý do Người nói trong ví dụ dừng lại trước khi giải thích lý do, khiến phần chuyển ý khó theo dõi hơn. Bằng chứng từ cách nói 00:00 / 00:13 Dòng thời gian bằng chứng ▶ Phát âm thanh mẫu ↺ Đặt lại âm thanh Tốc độ phát 1× 2× Âm thanh mẫu minh họa — không phải bản ghi của học viên. Giọng đọc do AI tạo (giọng tổng hợp). Nhấn phát: transcript và các mốc chạy theo âm thanh. 00:00 Trả lời 00:02 Lý do 00:08 Ví dụ Transcript minh họa Should people pay more for environmentally friendly products? Trả lời I think paying a little more can make sense. Điều nhiều khả năng đang giữ bạn lại: Khoảng dừng dài hơn khi chuyển từ ý kiến sang lý do: ưu tiên nhiều khả năng là cấu trúc, không phải từ vựng. Bài luyện tiếp theo: Answer → Reason → Example Thử bài luyện này → Dữ liệu mẫu minh họa · Không phải điểm IELTS chính thức Phương pháp Score-First và Solution-First Điểm số cho bạn biết mình đang ở đâu. Giải pháp cho bạn biết nên làm gì tiếp theo. Phản hồi tập trung vào điểm số Ước tính band Danh sách lỗi Lời khuyên chung Bạn tự chọn điều cần sửa Phản hồi Solution-First của Jurassic Ước tính luyện tập Bằng chứng từ chính lời bạn Mẫu vấn đề nhiều khả năng Một ưu tiên Một bài luyện cụ thể Kèm 1-1 cùng thầy Jay Biến ưu tiên tiếp theo thành buổi luyện tập trọng tâm. Mang báo cáo của bạn đến buổi học 1 kèm 1 qua Google Meet cùng đội ngũ giáo viên IELTS chuyên nghiệp của thầy Jay. Khám phá buổi học 1 kèm 1 → Dịch vụ riêng, tách biệt với bài thi thử AI. Không hứa hẹn điểm band. Ví dụ minh họa Hãy xem sự khác biệt Tập trung vào điểm số “Fluency & Coherence 6.0. Giảm khoảng dừng, dùng thêm từ nối, mở rộng vốn từ.” Solution-First “Khoảng dừng dài nhất (2,9 giây) nằm giữa ý kiến và lý do của bạn. Hãy luyện Answer → Reason → Example với câu hỏi mới.” Khung tư duy Khung A-R-E: Một cách đơn giản để xây dựng câu trả lời A Answer Nêu quan điểm rõ ràng trước. R Reason Giải thích vì sao bạn nghĩ vậy. E Example Làm ý tưởng trở nên cụ thể. Một khung tư duy, không phải bài mẫu: câu hỏi quyết định câu trả lời. Cách hoạt động Vòng lặp giải pháp 5 bước 01 / 05 Speak Trả lời theo thời gian kiểu IELTS. 02 / 05 Understand Xem bằng chứng. 03 / 05 Restructure Tìm mẫu vấn đề đang giới hạn bạn. 04 / 05 Practise Luyện một thay đổi. 05 / 05 Reassess Thử lại với câu hỏi mới. Minh bạch Rõ ràng về điều AI có thể, và không thể, cho bạn biết Không tâng bốc, không nói quá Mỗi ước tính band đều dẫn về một câu trích nguyên văn từ câu trả lời của bạn, và lượt rà soát thứ hai có thể giữ nguyên hoặc hạ band, không bao giờ nâng lên. Thể hiện mức độ không chắc chắn Mỗi ước tính đi kèm một khoảng điểm. Đây không bao giờ là điểm chính thức hay được bảo đảm. Bộ tự học Tự luyện, sửa từng thói quen một Bộ IELTS Speaking Ladder 390.000₫ bộ tự học · kèm One-to-One Starter 490.000₫ Xem mẫu → Tất cả bộ tài liệu IELTS → Gói lượt Trả theo báo cáo, không trả theo tháng Báo cáo Cơ bản dùng 1 lượt, Trung cấp 2 lượt, Nâng cao 3 lượt. Lượt có giá trị 12 tháng. Gói lượt Bài thi thử khởi đầu 79.000₫ Gói chẩn đoán 199.000₫ Gói luyện tập 10 lượt 549.000₫ Xem các gói lượt → SẮP RA MẮT · KÈM 1-1 & LUYỆN TẬP IELTS Writing Task 2 — Lập luận dựa trên bằng chứng Thôi học thuộc những khuôn bài luận cứng nhắc mà giám khảo đánh giá thấp. Học cách xây dựng bài Task 2 dài 250 từ, độc đáo và đạt điểm cao bằng thói quen đặc trưng Point + Proof + Explain (Luận điểm + Dẫn chứng + Giải thích). Phân tích đề trong 5 phút Làm chủ Coherence & Cohesion ở mức Band 7.0–8.5 Mở rộng dẫn chứng từ thực tế Nhận xét chi tiết theo từng tiêu chí Đăng ký danh sách chờ luyện Viết (info@jurassicenglish.com) → Học 1 kèm 1 → Jurassic English ™ AI Speaking · Luyện Nói theo định dạng IELTS Đọc sách & Phiêu lưu truyện Nói & IELTS cho teen Luyện IELTS cho người lớn IELTS Writing Task 2 (Sắp ra mắt) Đánh giá Nói trực tiếp Khung học thuật Quyền riêng tư Điều khoản Thành viên của WorldWise Learning : worldwiselearning.app · info@jurassicenglish.com Jurassic English™ là đơn vị giáo dục độc lập do WorldWise Learning vận hành tại Hà Nội, Việt Nam (info@jurassicenglish.com, Zalo/Điện thoại +84 396 085 076), không liên kết với và không được IELTS, IDP, British Council hay Cambridge bảo trợ. Các mức band là ước tính để huấn luyện, không bao giờ là điểm thi chính thức được bảo đảm. Câu trả lời của bạn (bản nhập, hoặc nội dung văn bản của câu trả lời bằng giọng nói) được gửi đến nhà cung cấp AI chấm điểm ở ngoài Việt Nam, được nêu tên trước khi bạn bắt đầu; nội dung văn bản và báo cáo được lưu 30 ngày để xem lại, sau đó tự động xóa. Với người dùng được mời tham gia beta giọng nói, bản ghi âm đi qua dịch vụ xử lý của chúng tôi trên Vercel tại Singapore đến Microsoft Azure Speech (Singapore) và không bao giờ được chúng tôi lưu trữ. Chúng tôi không bao giờ bán dữ liệu cá nhân của bạn; chi tiết đầy đủ có trong Thông báo quyền riêng tư của AI Speaking. Thông báo quyền riêng tư → Jurassic AI Speaking cung cấp phản hồi luyện tập do AI tạo. Đây không phải điểm IELTS chính thức và không được dùng làm căn cứ chính thức cho việc chấm điểm, xếp lớp, tuyển sinh hay tuyển dụng. Phát âm không được đánh giá qua văn bản nhập; ở chế độ nói (beta), phát âm là ước tính luyện tập dựa trên các chỉ số đang thử nghiệm. Không cam kết bất kỳ điểm số hay band nào. يشترط القبول في الدراسات العليا بالجامعة الأمريكية بالقاهرة (AUC) ايلتس الأكاديمي بدرجة إجمالية 6.5 مع 7.0 في الكتابة، وقد تطلب بعض البرامج أكثر من ذلك. والتدريب على المحادثة منفصل عن استيفاء شرط الكتابة. اقرأ الشرط أو البيانات المنشورة. يوضّح الحد الأدنى للكتابة في الدراسات العليا بـ AUC لماذا لا تكفي الدرجة الإجمالية لايلتس وحدها لحسم الطلب. راجع شروط الدراسات العليا كاملةً، ثم تأكّد مما إذا كانت درجتك العلمية تحديدًا تضيف شروطًا أخرى. وإذا كنت تستعد للهجرة، فراجع قائمة الاختبارات المعتمدة لدى تلك الجهة بدلًا من ذلك. ماذا تعني أدلة المحادثة الهدف المحدد للقبول أكثر فائدة من ادّعاء عام عن المتحدثين المصريين. افحص المكوّنات التي تطلبها المؤسسة المستقبِلة فعلًا. يمكن لتسجيل صوتي لمتقدّم مصري أن يكشف ما إذا كانت الإجابة تدعم فكرتها الرئيسية. اطلب من المعلّم أن يشير إلى جملة أو وقفة بعينها ويشرح أثرها في الوضوح. ولا تقول هذه الملاحظة شيئًا مؤكدًا عن أي درجة رسمية. تسلسل تدريب للمتعلمين في مصر استخدم إجابتك المنقّحة عن اهتماماتك البحثية نقطةَ انطلاق فقط. ثم أجب عن سؤال حول مشروع خارج تخصصك. فإذا ظللت قادرًا على ربط مثال بسبب، فلديك دليل على تغيير مفيد في تدريبك. تنشر الجامعة البريطانية في مصر (BUE) مسارًا للإعفاء من اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية الخاص بها لمرحلة البكالوريوس بدرجة 5.0 في ايلتس الأكاديمي. تأكّد من مسار القبول الذي ينطبق عليك. راجع المسار الرسمي. وحجز جلسة تدريب لا يحلّ أبدًا محلّ قواعد الجهة المستقبِلة. طرق التدريب المتاحة تقييم المحادثة المباشر الأوّلي المدفوع فحصٌ أوّلي قصير، ويمكن للدروس التي يقودها المعلّم أن تعالج المشكلة التي يُظهرها التسجيل. ويناسب تدريب المحادثة بالذكاء الاصطناعي للبالغين (18+) الأوقاتَ خارج الجلسات المجدولة، مع أن اقتراحاته قد تكون غير دقيقة. يمكن للمتقدّم أن يحتفظ بقائمتَي تحقّق مختلفتين: واحدة للقبول في الدراسات العليا بـ AUC ، وأخرى لوجهة منفصلة في الخارج. لا تفترض أن صيغة ايلتس نفسها أو الحد الأدنى نفسه ينطبق على الاثنتين. وفي جلستك، تدرّب على شرح هدفك الأكاديمي بلغة بسيطة، واسأل عن الجزء الذي لا يزال غير واضح للمستمع. تختلف متطلبات البرامج في مصر تنشر إدارة القبول للدراسات العليا في AUC شرط ايلتس الأكاديمي بدرجة إجمالية 6.5 مع 7.0 في الكتابة، وتشير إلى أن بعض البرامج قد تشترط أكثر. وتقبل نتيجة One Skill Retake (إعادة مهارة واحدة) موثّقة وفق الشروط التي تحددها. ويحتاج طالب الدراسات العليا المحتمل إلى صفحة البرنامج إلى جانب صفحة القبول العامة. يمكن لتدريب المحادثة أن يساعد في الإجابة الشفهية، لكن الحد الأدنى للكتابة يجب التعامل معه بشكل منفصل. أما الجامعة البريطانية في مصر فتصف مسارًا مختلفًا لمرحلة البكالوريوس: إذ يجوز إعفاء المتقدمين المؤهَّلين من حملة الثانوية العامة من اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية الخاص بها إذا كانت لديهم نتيجة سارية في ايلتس الأكاديمي بدرجة 5.0 ، بينما تضع تلك الصفحة شرط ايلتس 5.0 لحملة الشهادات الدولية. هذا مثال على القبول المحلي، وليس قاعدة من قواعد AUC . حدّد فئة المتقدمين التي تنطبق عليك قبل أن تعتبر الرقم المذكور هدفًا لك. صيغ الاختبار والأدلة للمتقدم من مصر تتضمّن قوائم مراكز IDP في مصر اختبارَي الأكاديمي والتدريب العام على الكمبيوتر، وخيارًا على الكمبيوتر يُؤدّى فيه قسم الكتابة على الورق، وايلتس لأغراض UKVI ، وايلتس Life Skills ، و One Skill Retake . ومن المدن المدرجة: القاهرة والجيزة والإسكندرية وطنطا والمنصورة. وعلى من يفضّل الكتابة بخط اليد أن يتأكد من الجلسة المحددة، بدلًا من افتراض أن كل مركز للاختبار على الكمبيوتر يقدّم خيار الكتابة نفسه. ويجب أيضًا أن تقبل المؤسسة المستقبِلة الاختبار المختار وأي إعادة له. بالنسبة إلى نظام Express Entry الكندي، تشترط IRCC اختبار التدريب العام (General Training) وتستبعد One Skill Retake . وهذا يختلف عن المسار الأكاديمي في AUC . وتُفيد بيانات ielts.org الأكاديمية لعام 2024–25 بأن متوسط المحادثة لمصر بلغ 6.65 والمتوسط العام 6.67 . وبلغ متوسط القراءة 7.07 والكتابة 6.10 في صف الجنسية نفسه. لا يمكن لهذه الأرقام الجماعية أن تحدّد أهلية المتقدم لبرنامج ما ولا احتياجه الشخصي في التدريب. وتنص AUC على أن نتيجة الاختبار الأكاديمي يجب أن تظل سارية حتى أول يوم دراسي. ويهمّ هذا التوقيت عندما يختار المتقدم للدراسات العليا موعد الاختبار، خاصةً إذا كان البرنامج يضع شروطًا إضافية أيضًا. أسئلة من مصر هل يمكنني التحضير عبر الإنترنت من مصر؟ نعم. يمكن للبالغين في مصر ترتيب درس عبر الإنترنت بعد التحقق من الساعة المعروضة وتعليمات الدفع. هل رسوم اختبار ايلتس المحلية مشمولة في التدريب؟ لا. يتقاضى مركز الاختبار في مصر رسوم ايلتس، بينما تتقاضى Jurassic English رسوم التدريب بشكل مستقل. هل تُحتسب ملاحظات التدريب نتيجةً لايلتس؟ لا. تقرّر AUC والجهات المستقبِلة الأخرى أيّ نتيجة رسمية تقبلها. بأيّ توقيت يظهر موعد الحجز؟ يظهر الموعد بتوقيت هانوي؛ والساعة في مصر متأخرة عنه بخمس ساعات وفق الجدول المذكور. قبل أن تحجز تحقّق من الصيغة التي اخترتها لدى المزوّد في مصر، خاصةً إذا كنت تريد الكتابة على الورق مع اختبار على الكمبيوتر. وتأكّد من الشروط الحالية للمؤسسة المستقبِلة، وحوّل ساعة الحجز بتوقيت هانوي إلى توقيت مصر. أي تقدير تدريبي ليس درجة ايلتس رسمية. كما أن Jurassic English مستقلة عن British Council و IDP IELTS و Cambridge University Press & Assessment . ولا يحدّد التدريب الأهلية للقبول أو التسجيل المهني أو الهجرة. اقرأ أيضًا الأكاديمية في السعودية المتوسط العام في إحصاءات ايلتس المرتبطة. ومع ذلك، يجعل شرط البرنامج التحضيري في جامعة الفيصل أداءَ كل متقدم بنفسه أهمَّ من أي متوسط. قد يشرح المتحدث موضوعًا مألوفًا بارتياح، لكنه يفقد ترابط كلامه عندما يطلب منه الممتحِن إجراء مقارنة. وتُظهر عيّنة محادثة واحدة أين يحدث ذلك. يمكن للمعلّم أن يعلّم طريقة لتنظيم الفكرة التالية، وأن يدرّب عليها بتوجيه، ثم يتحقق من إجابة جديدة. تقرّر KAUST والجهات المستقبِلة الأخرى أي نتيجة رسمية تقبلها؛ ولا يحسم تسجيل التدريب قرار القبول. كيف يعمل التدريب عبر الإنترنت للمتعلم في السعودية إن كنت تسعى إلى إنهاء البرنامج التحضيري في جامعة الفيصل، فأحضِر متطلباته المنشورة؛ وإن كانت KAUST هدفك، فأحضِر صفحة القبول في الدراسات العليا لديها. يبدأ المعلّم بمحاولة محادثة غير مُعدّة مسبقًا، ويشخّص سمة واحدة يمكن تحسينها. اتفقا على أولوية، وطوّر طريقة للمقارنة بين الأفكار أو شرحها، وتدرّب بصوت مسموع. جرّب سؤالًا جديدًا باستقلالية لإعادة قياس تلك السمة. تسجيلاتك أنت دليل تدريبي أفضل من المتوسط الوطني في السعودية. تحقّق مع الجامعة إن كنت تعتمد على قائمة اعتراف استرشادية؛ فالدرس لا يستطيع تحويل تلك القائمة إلى قرار قبول مؤكَّد. لإجراء أول تقييم مباشر، اطّلع على تقييم المحادثة المباشر الأوّلي المدفوع . ولمواصلة العمل بقيادة المعلّم، راجع خيارات التدريب الفردي . ويمكن للبالغين (18+) أيضًا استخدام تدريب المحادثة بالذكاء الاصطناعي بين الدروس. قد تخطئ ملاحظات الذكاء الاصطناعي؛ لذا تحقّق من النصائح المهمة بمقارنتها بملاحظات بشرية وبمعايير التقييم الرسمية المنشورة للعموم. أسئلة من هذا السوق هل يمكن لايلتس أن يستوفي شرط إنهاء البرنامج التحضيري في جامعة الفيصل؟ تُدرج صفحة جامعة الفيصل التي راجعناها ايلتس إلى جانب متطلبات أخرى لإنهاء البرنامج التحضيري الجامعي. هل تعفي KAUST من شرط اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية؟ تذكر صفحة التقديم للدراسات العليا لديها أنه لا توجد استثناءات؛ تحقّق من الأدلة المقبولة لديها حاليًا. هل درجات الاعتراف الخاصة بجامعة الملك سعود نهائية؟ تصفها صفحة ايلتس بأنها استرشادية. تأكّد من الجامعة. أي صيغة اختبار في السعودية ينبغي أن أختار؟ تُدرج الجهات المزوّدة التي راجعناها عدة صيغ؛ تحقّق من توافرها في موعدك وبما يناسب غرضك. قبل أن تحجز قارن مواعيد اختبارات IDP و British Council الحالية في السعودية للصيغة التي تحتاجها. تحقّق من قاعدة القبول أو البرنامج التحضيري في جامعتك، بما في ذلك أي شروط تتجاوز ايلتس. حوّل موعد الحجز بتوقيت هانوي إلى توقيت السعودية، وتحقّق من اتصال الصوت لديك. أحضِر محاولة محادثة جديدة بدلًا من إجابة مكتوبة مصقولة. أي تقدير تدريبي ليس درجة ايلتس رسمية. كما أن Jurassic English الحالي لا يحدّد درجة فرعية لايلتس في البند الذي راجعناه. اسأل مكتب القبول إن كان هناك شرط أكثر تفصيلًا. تساعدك هذه التحققات على اختيار هدف عملي في المحادثة من دون افتراض أن تقدير التدريب أو المتوسط متابعة الشرح، لا مما إذا كانت الإجابة تشبه نموذجًا محفوظًا. افصل بين شروط التوظيف وقواعد القبول الجامعي، واسأل الجهة المستقبِلة عن أي أمر لا توضّحه صفحتها. لإجراء أول تقييم مباشر، اطّلع على تقييم title: Curriculum Coherence Audit Sprint | Jurassic English™
h1: The Curriculum Coherence Audit Sprint.
description: A focused curriculum review for schools and centers: alignment, materials, teacher practice, progression logic, and an implementation roadmap.
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices English EN Tiếng Việt Tiếng Việt Free sample pack Free sample pack Back to main site Institutional Entry Point 10 Business Days The Curriculum Coherence Audit Sprint. A structured 10-business-day diagnostic of your current English programme — curriculum alignment, teacher practice, materials quality, and progression logic — delivered as a formal gap analysis with a clear implementation roadmap. Request Your Audit Sprint Book a Discovery Call Why Programmes Underperform Most English programmes are not failing because of effort. They are failing because of architecture. Capable teachers, reasonable materials, and genuine commitment are not enough when the underlying programme lacks coherence. Without a structured review, the same gaps recur year after year. Standards Drift Programmes that were once CEFR-aligned gradually drift as materials are swapped, teachers change, and institutional memory erodes. Alignment becomes assumed rather than verified. Inconsistent Delivery When curriculum design lives inside individual teachers rather than in a shared framework, quality depends entirely on who is in the room. That is not a scalable or auditable model. Invisible Progression Gaps Students plateau not because they lack ability, but because the programme has no coherent progression logic — no structured movement from comprehension to reasoning to justification. Who This Is For Built for the people responsible for programme quality. The Audit Sprint is designed for institutional leaders who need evidence, not opinions — and a clear picture of what the right next step looks like. SME Centre Owners Know exactly where your programme stands — and what it would take to differentiate it. If your centre competes on price rather than method, an Audit Sprint gives you the evidence to justify a repositioning. You leave with a documented picture of your programme's current state and a concrete pathway to standards alignment. title: অনলাইন IELTS Speaking কোচিং – বাংলাদেশ | Jurassic English™
h1: বাংলাদেশের শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য অনলাইন IELTS Speaking কোচিং
description: বাংলাদেশের প্রাপ্তবয়স্কদের জন্য ওয়ান-টু-ওয়ান অনলাইন IELTS Speaking কোচিং, Mr. Jay Adams (CELTA)-এর নেতৃত্বে। ৬০ মিনিট US$35, প্রাথমিক মূল্যায়ন US$29।
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices Book Baseline · US$29 Baseline · US$29 বাংলাদেশ বাংলাদেশের শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য অনলাইন IELTS Speaking কোচিং কেউ যুক্তরাজ্যে পড়ার সুযোগ খুঁজছেন; আবার কেউ দেখছেন স্থানীয় ভর্তি পরীক্ষা মওকুফ হতে পারে কি না। এই পৃষ্ঠাটি বাংলাদেশের প্রাপ্তবয়স্কদের জন্য স্থানীয় পরীক্ষার তথ্যকে অনলাইন Speaking অনুশীলনের সঙ্গে যুক্ত করে। সবসময় শুরু করুন স্কোর গ্রহণকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রকাশিত শর্ত দিয়ে। বাংলা English CELTA Mr. Jay Adams প্রাথমিক Speaking মূল্যায়নের অনুরোধ করুন · US$29 একান্ত পাঠের অনুরোধ করুন · US$35 / 60 মিনিট অনুরোধ যায় info@jurassicenglish.com-এ। USD-তে কার্ড পেমেন্ট এখনও চালু হয়নি। আগে একটি নমুনা রিপোর্ট দেখুন (ইংরেজিতে) → শেখার উপকরণ বুকিংয়ের আগে মূল তথ্য কে পড়ান: Mr. Jay Adams (CELTA) হ্যানয় থেকে Jurassic English পরিচালনা করেন। অনলাইন ক্লাসগুলো নেন Mr. Jay-এর পেশাদার IELTS শিক্ষকদের দল। স্থানীয় পরীক্ষা: IDP Bangladesh কম্পিউটারে নেওয়া Academic ও General Training পরীক্ষার বিকল্প এবং আলাদা IELTS for UKVI পরীক্ষা প্রকাশ করে। নিচের ফি তাদের সাধারণ কম্পিউটার-ভিত্তিক পরীক্ষার জন্য। স্থানীয় Academic পরীক্ষার ফি: BDT 31,100, পরীক্ষা পরিচালনাকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের ফি পৃষ্ঠা থেকে নেওয়া, 14 অক্টোবর 2026-এ যাচাই করা। বর্তমান পরিমাণ সরাসরি নিশ্চিত করে নিন। সময়: হ্যানয়ের বুকিংয়ে ভিয়েতনামের সময় (UTC+7) দেখানো হয়। বাংলাদেশ হ্যানয়ের চেয়ে 1 ঘণ্টা পিছিয়ে। নিশ্চিত করার আগে দেখানো সময়টি বাংলাদেশের সময়ে রূপান্তর করে নিন। আমাদের মূল্য: ওয়ান-টু-ওয়ান অনলাইন কোচিং: প্রতি 60 মিনিটে US$35। 8 পাঠের প্যাক: US$245, 35 দিন বৈধ। Live Speaking Baseline: US$29 (প্রায় 15–20 মিনিট)। পেমেন্ট: দাম মার্কিন ডলারে। আন্তর্জাতিক কার্ড পেমেন্ট শিগগিরই চালু হবে; ততদিন বুক করতে আমাদের সঙ্গে যোগাযোগ করুন । সঠিক IELTS পথ বেছে নিন North South University জানায়, ভর্তির অন্যান্য শর্ত পূরণ হলে IELTS 7.0 স্কোর দিয়ে তাদের ভর্তি পরীক্ষা মওকুফ হতে পারে। এটি একটি মওকুফের শর্ত, ভর্তির সাধারণ ব্যান্ড নয়। প্রকাশিত শর্ত বা তথ্য পড়ুন। NSU-র মওকুফ আর যুক্তরাজ্যে পড়ার আবেদন দুটি আলাদা সিদ্ধান্ত। প্রতিটি ভর্তি নিয়ম পুরোটা পড়ুন, IELTS-এর সংখ্যার বাইরের শর্তগুলোসহ। পরীক্ষা পরিচালনাকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানে পরীক্ষা বুক করলেই প্রমাণ হয় না যে আবেদনকারী কোনো একটি পথের জন্য যোগ্য। Speaking-এর প্রমাণ আসলে কী বোঝায় IELTS-এর তথ্য অনুযায়ী 2024–25 সালে বাংলাদেশি Academic পরীক্ষার্থীদের Speaking গড় 5.88 এবং সামগ্রিক গড় 6.00। এগুলো দলগত পরিসংখ্যান; একটি ক্লাসের জন্য আপনার রেকর্ড করা উত্তর বেশি প্রাসঙ্গিক প্রমাণ দেয়। IELTS পরীক্ষার্থীদের পারফরম্যান্স ডেটা Speaking ক্লাসে এমন একটি প্রশ্ন নিয়ে আসুন, যার উত্তর আপনি সময়ের চাপে দিয়েছেন। শিক্ষক খেয়াল করতে পারেন আপনি কীভাবে একটি পরিবর্তনের কথা তোলেন, তার ফলাফল ব্যাখ্যা করেন এবং পরের প্রশ্ন সামলান। এই কাজে সব পরীক্ষার্থীর গড়ের চেয়ে একটি রেকর্ড করা নমুনা বেশি কাজে আসে। বাংলাদেশের শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য অনুশীলনের ধাপ একটি নির্দেশিত অনুশীলনের পর রেকর্ডিংটি আবার শুনুন। এমন একটি বাক্য চিহ্নিত করুন যা এখন একটি প্রভাব স্পষ্টভাবে বোঝায়, আর এমন একটি বাক্য যার এখনও একটি উদাহরণ দরকার। তারপর একটি অপরিচিত বিষয়ে কথা বলুন এবং দেখুন একই যুক্তি নিজে নিজে প্রয়োগ করতে পারেন কি না। আপনার আবেদনে মওকুফ প্রযোজ্য কি না, তা NSU-কে জিজ্ঞেস করুন। বিদেশে পড়ার জন্য গন্তব্য প্রোগ্রামের নিজস্ব স্কোরের শর্ত পড়ুন। একটি অনুশীলন সেশন বুক করা কখনোই স্কোর গ্রহণকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিয়মের বিকল্প নয়। অনুশীলনের যে উপায়গুলো আছে অল্প সময়ের একটি লাইভ সূচনা চাইলে, পেইড Baseline একটি সীমিত অনুশীলন নমুনা রেকর্ড করে। ওয়ান-টু-ওয়ান ক্লাসে আরও নির্দেশিত Speaking অনুশীলন হয়। 18 বছর বা তার বেশি বয়সী প্রাপ্তবয়স্করা অন্য সময়ে AI Speaking টুল ব্যবহার করতে পারেন; এর পরামর্শ অনুযায়ী কিছু করার আগে তা যাচাই করে নিন। স্থানীয় পরীক্ষা মওকুফ প্রাসঙ্গিক হলে, IELTS-কে ভর্তি পরীক্ষার বিকল্প হিসেবে ধরার আগে ভর্তির পুরো শর্ত নিশ্চিত করুন। Speaking অনুশীলনের সময় এমন একটি প্রশ্ন বেছে নিন যেখানে তুলনা করতে হয়। একটি পার্থক্য ও তার ফলাফল ব্যাখ্যা করুন, তারপর একই যুক্তি একটি নতুন বিষয়ে প্রকাশ করার চেষ্টা করুন। বাংলাদেশে পরীক্ষা বুকিং আসলে কী কী অন্তর্ভুক্ত করে IDP Bangladesh তাদের বিভিন্ন কেন্দ্রে, যেমন ঢাকা, চট্টগ্রাম, সিলেট, খুলনা ও রাজশাহীতে, কম্পিউটারে নেওয়া Academic ও General Training পরীক্ষার তালিকা দেয়। তারা IELTS for UKVI, Life Skills এবং One Skill Retake পরীক্ষাও তালিকাভুক্ত করে। এই নামগুলো আবেদনের ভিন্ন ভিন্ন উদ্দেশ্য নির্দেশ করে। একজন পরীক্ষার্থীর উচিত প্রথমে জেনে নেওয়া, ফলাফল গ্রহণকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান বা কর্তৃপক্ষ কোন পরীক্ষা গ্রহণ করে, তারপর সেই অনুযায়ী পরীক্ষা ও কেন্দ্র বেছে নেওয়া। North South University-তে ভর্তির কথা ভাবছেন এমন ঢাকার একজন আবেদনকারীর উচিত প্রকাশিত আন্ডারগ্র্যাজুয়েট মওকুফ নিয়ম মনোযোগ দিয়ে পড়া: ভর্তির অন্যান্য শর্ত পূরণ হলে, নির্দিষ্ট BA in English এবং BSS Media, Communication & Journalism প্রোগ্রামের ক্ষেত্রে IELTS 7.0 ভর্তি পরীক্ষা মওকুফ করতে পারে। এটি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে ভর্তির সাধারণ স্কোর নয়। একটি কোচিং সেশনে আলোচনার বিষয় হতে পারে, আবেদনকারী তাঁর কোর্স বেছে নেওয়ার কারণ কতটা স্পষ্টভাবে ব্যাখ্যা করেন; মওকুফের আনুষ্ঠানিক সিদ্ধান্ত NSU-রই। যুক্তরাজ্যে পড়াশোনা ও জাতীয় পরিসংখ্যান যুক্তরাজ্য সরকারের তথ্য অনুযায়ী ডিসেম্বর 2025-এ শেষ হওয়া বছরে বাংলাদেশি নাগরিকদের 10,828টি স্পনসরড স্টাডি ভিসা দেওয়া হয়েছে, যা আগের বছরের চেয়ে 71% বেশি। এটি যুক্তরাজ্যে পড়ার আগ্রহ বোঝাতে সাহায্য করে, কিন্তু এর মানে এই নয় যে বাংলাদেশি শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য একটিই IELTS শর্ত আছে। গন্তব্য ডিগ্রি একটি সামগ্রিক স্কোরের পাশাপাশি প্রতিটি অংশের আলাদা ন্যূনতম স্কোর চাইতে পারে। পরীক্ষার ফি দেওয়ার আগে দুটোই লিখে রাখুন। ielts.org-এর 2024–25 Academic পারফরম্যান্স ফাইল অনুযায়ী বাংলাদেশের Speaking গড় 5.88 এবং সামগ্রিক গড় 6.00। একই জাতীয়তার সারিতে Reading 6.23, Listening 5.82 এবং Writing 5.83। এগুলো দলগত গড়; একজন শিক্ষার্থীর নিজের রেকর্ডিং আর আনুষ্ঠানিক টেস্ট রিপোর্ট ভিন্ন ধরনের প্রমাণ। অনুশীলনের কাজ বাছাই করতে নিজের কথা বলার নমুনা ব্যবহার করুন, আর ভর্তির শর্ত যাচাই করতে আনুষ্ঠানিক ফলাফল ব্যবহার করুন। বাংলাদেশের শিক্ষার্থীদের প্রশ্ন আমি কি বাংলাদেশ থেকে অনলাইনে প্রস্তুতি নিতে পারি? হ্যাঁ। হ্যানয়ের সময়সূচি এবং তালিকাভুক্ত পেমেন্ট পদ্ধতি আপনার জন্য সুবিধাজনক হলে বাংলাদেশের প্রাপ্তবয়স্করা অনলাইন ক্লাসের অনুরোধ করতে পারেন। স্থানীয় IELTS পরীক্ষার ফি কি কোচিংয়ের মধ্যে অন্তর্ভুক্ত? না। BDT-তে নেওয়া পরীক্ষার ফি পরীক্ষা পরিচালনাকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রাপ্য; কোচিংয়ের মূল্য আলাদাভাবে নেওয়া হয়। অনুশীলনের ফিডব্যাক কি IELTS ফলাফল হিসেবে গণ্য হয়? না। NSU বা যুক্তরাজ্যের কোনো কোর্স তাদের নির্ধারিত প্রমাণই চায়, ক্লাসের কোনো আনুমানিক মূল্যায়ন নয়। বুকিংয়ে কোন সময় দেখানো হয়? হ্যানয় বাংলাদেশের চেয়ে এক ঘণ্টা এগিয়ে; বুক করার আগে রূপান্তরিত তারিখ ও সময় মিলিয়ে নিন। বুক করার আগে আপনার বেছে নেওয়া বাংলাদেশের কেন্দ্রের আনুষ্ঠানিক ফি নিশ্চিত করুন এবং আপনার একাডেমিক রেকর্ডের ক্ষেত্রে মওকুফ প্রযোজ্য কি না, তা ভর্তি অফিসকে জিজ্ঞেস করুন। কোচিংয়ের ফি দেওয়ার আগে দেখানো হ্যানয়ের ক্লাসের সময় বাংলাদেশের সময়ের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে নিন। অনুশীলনের যেকোনো আনুমানিক মূল্যায়ন আনুষ্ঠানিক IELTS স্কোর নয়। Jurassic English একটি স্বতন্ত্র প্রতিষ্ঠান; British Council, IDP IELTS এবং Cambridge University Press & Assessment-এর সঙ্গে এর কোনো সম্পর্ক নেই। কোচিং ভর্তি, পেশাগত নিবন্ধন বা অভিবাসনের যোগ্যতা নির্ধারণ করে না। আরও পড়ুন IELTS Speaking 6 থেকে 7 গাইড IELTS অনলাইন টেস্ট গাইড IELTS ব্যান্ড স্কোর ক্যালকুলেটর Speaking Part 2 টাইমার আন্তর্জাতিক কোচিং হাব শিক্ষকের সঙ্গে অনুশীলনে প্রস্তুত? প্রাথমিক Speaking মূল্যায়নের অনুরোধ করুন · US$29 AI দিয়ে Speaking অনুশীলন কীভাবে কাজ করে (18+, ইংরেজিতে) বিনামূল্যে IELTS ব্যান্ড ক্যালকুলেটর (ইংরেজিতে) অনুরোধ যায় info@jurassicenglish.com-এ। USD-তে কার্ড পেমেন্ট এখনও চালু হয়নি। Jurassic English ™ Reading & Story Adventures Story Club (ages 5–8) Speaking & Teen IELTS Adult IELTS Practice IELTS Coaching by Country IELTS Writing Task 2 (Coming Soon) Live Speaking Baseline Academic Framework Products & prices Privacy Terms Contact For schools Knowledge Hub Curriculum Series Thinking Cycle School Framework Digital Reasoning Engine For Companies Looking for university AI governance, Circular 54 readiness, or school curriculum licensing? title: CEFR Alignment, CEFR-V and MOET 2030 — Curriculum Standards Architecture | Jurassic English™
h1: Standards alignment is not a badge. It is a documented architectural decision.
description: How Jurassic English™ and WorldWise Learning map to CEFR, CEFR-V, and MOET 2030 national standards. A standards-facing companion to the methodology page — for institutional procurement, accreditation, and compliance review.
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices English EN Tiếng Việt Tiếng Việt Free sample pack Free sample pack Back to main site Standards Architecture CEFR · CEFR-V · MOET 2030 Standards alignment is not a badge. It is a documented architectural decision. Any programme can label its levels A1 through C1. Genuine CEFR alignment requires that the curriculum is structurally built around communicative competence progression — and that the evidence for that alignment can be audited, documented, and defended to a procurement committee. Request an Audit Sprint Book a Discovery Call The Alignment Gap Most programmes claim CEFR alignment. Far fewer can demonstrate it. The difference between claimed and structural alignment is the difference between a marketing statement and a defensible curriculum architecture. Procurement committees, accreditation bodies, and government regulators are increasingly able to tell them apart. Label Alignment vs. Structural Alignment Labelling a coursebook unit "B1" without mapping the tasks, assessment criteria, and progression logic to B1 communicative competence descriptors is decoration, not architecture. CEFR levels are descriptions of learner capability — not headings for textbook chapters. Grammar-First vs. Competence-First CEFR is a framework for communicative competence — what a learner can do with language — not a grammar syllabus with level labels. Programmes that organise progression around tense sequences and vocabulary lists while calling it CEFR-aligned have misread the framework. International Standards vs. Local Requirements CEFR alignment is necessary but insufficient in Vietnam. CEFR-V and the MOET 2030 National English Language Programme introduce specific institutional obligations — progression targets, teacher qualification standards, and compliance documentation requirements — that generic CEFR maps do not address. What CEFR Actually Requires Communicative competence, not linguistic inventory. The Common European Framework of Reference for Languages describes what learners can do with language across five domains: reading, listening, spoken interaction, spoken production, and writing. Progression through CEFR levels is a progression in communicative capability and cognitive complexity — not simply in vocabulary range or grammatical accuracy. CEFR Domain Reading Ability to understand and critically process written texts of increasing complexity, authorial intent, and argumentative structure. How the Thinking Cycle addresses this The Analyze stage of the Thinking Cycle directly develops CEFR reading competence — not just comprehension, but interrogation of how and why a text is constructed. CEFR Domain Spoken Interaction Ability to engage in structured academic dialogue — building on another's argument, challenging positions with evidence, and defending a reasoned stance. How the Thinking Cycle addresses this Socratic seminar and structured debate protocols are embedded from Level 2 onward, developing the spontaneity and precision that higher CEFR levels require. CEFR Domain Writing Ability to produce organised, evidence-based written argument — moving from simple justification sentences at A1 to research-quality extended essays at C1. How the Thinking Cycle addresses this The Justify stage produces structured academic writing at every level. The CEIW framework (Claim, Evidence, Interpretation, Warrant) scaffolds progression from single sentence to multi-paragraph to extended essay. The Jurassic English™ curriculum is built around CEFR CAN-DO descriptors at every level — not retrofitted to them after design. The Vietnam Standards Context CEFR-V and MOET 2030 create institutional obligations that international CEFR maps do not cover. For schools, training centres, and institutional partners operating in Vietnam, standards compliance extends beyond general CEFR alignment. Two frameworks define the regulatory and procurement landscape. CEFR-V Vietnam Language Competency Framework (Khung năng lực ngoại ngữ 6 bậc) The official Vietnamese adaptation of CEFR, issued under Ministry of Education and Training Decision 01/2014/TT-BGDĐT. Six aligned levels from pre-A1 through C2. All public school English programmes are required to demonstrate CEFR-V alignment — not general CEFR alignment. Institutional implication Curriculum documentation submitted for institutional review or accreditation must reference CEFR-V descriptors specifically. MOET 2030 National English Language Education Project 2017–2030 The national programme requiring Vietnamese students to reach defined CEFR-V benchmarks by graduation. School graduates: minimum B1. University graduates: minimum B2. Teachers: minimum B2 (primary), C1 (secondary). Institutional programmes must demonstrate a credible pathway to these targets. Institutional implication Procurement committees at compliant institutions are now required to assess whether partner curricula can document progress toward MOET 2030 targets. WorldWise Learning's institutional curriculum is mapped to both CEFR-V and MOET 2030 targets. The Audit Sprint produces standards documentation formatted specifically for institutional review under these frameworks. Curriculum Progression Map Pre-A1 through C1. Five levels. One coherent architecture. Every Jurassic English™ level is mapped to CEFR communicative competence descriptors. Progression is determined by reasoning demand and text complexity — not simply vocabulary load or grammar scope. Level 1 01 Foundation Pre-A1 → A1 Ages 4–8 First justification writing: Claim + Evidence sentence structure Text interrogation through guided Analyze stage Moral reasoning about character choices in picture books Oral response using CEFR A1 spoken interaction frames View full level Level 2 02 Development A1 → A2 Ages 8–10 Point-Evidence-Comment paragraph structure introduced Evaluate stage: assessing argument quality in early chapter books Socratic dialogue protocols at A2 spoken interaction level Written justification responses across core text set View full level Level 3 03 Expansion A2 → B1 Ages 10–12 The Literacy Pivot: transition to complex chapter book analysis CEIW writing structure: Claim, Evidence, Interpretation, Warrant B1 reading competence: identifying implicit meaning and authorial intent Structured academic debate at B1 spoken production level View full level Level 4 04 Mastery B1 → B2 Ages 12–14 Novel analysis: contested texts with multiple interpretive positions Multi-paragraph academic essay to B2 written production standards Formal debate: position construction, rebuttal, cross-examination B2 reading: nuanced comprehension of abstract and contested argument View full level Level 5 05 Advanced B2 → C1 Ages 14+ Intertextual analysis: comparative reading across literary and critical texts Research essay to C1 extended writing standards IB Language A and Cambridge Literature preparation pathway C1 spoken: sustained academic argument with precision and register control View full level For Institutional Leaders Standards alignment serves different institutional needs depending on your role. The WorldWise Learning curriculum and Audit Sprint are designed to produce documentation that is useful to the people who have to defend programme quality — not just describe it. SME Centre Owners Documented alignment turns a positioning claim into a defensible competitive advantage. Parents and institutional clients increasingly ask for evidence of standards alignment — not just CEFR level labels. A programme that can produce documented CEFR-V alignment and a MOET 2030 progression pathway is positioned differently from one that cannot. CEFR-V alignment documentation for institutional marketing Progression evidence for parent and client enquiries Differentiation from test-prep category competitors Audit Sprint produces the documentation from your existing programme School Leaders and Principals Accreditation-ready standards documentation for committee and regulatory review. Whether your school is preparing for CEFR-V compliance under MOET 2030, applying for Cambridge or IB accreditation, or entering an internal programme review cycle, the evidence base required is the same: documented curriculum architecture, aligned to named standards, with a defensible progression logic. CEFR-V and MOET 2030 compliance documentation pathway Cambridge and IB alignment mapping Committee-formatted gap analysis and standards report WorldWise Learning partnership includes ongoing compliance support Academic Directors A shared standards framework that governs what happens across every classroom. Academic governance depends on having a curriculum framework that teachers can be measured against — not just a set of materials. CEFR-V alignment embedded in the curriculum architecture gives academic directors an auditable standard against which teacher practice and programme delivery can be assessed. Teacher practice alignment to CEFR-V competence descriptors Multi-level progression coherence across your full programme Assessment and moderation framework aligned to CEFR standards Audit Sprint outputs formatted for academic committee review Start with the Standards Conversation Know where your programme stands against the standards that matter. The Curriculum Coherence Audit Sprint is the most direct route to understanding your programme's current alignment posture — and what a documented pathway to CEFR-V and MOET 2030 compliance looks like in your specific institutional context. title: Literature-Based Critical Thinking Framework | Jurassic English™
h1: The deeper architecture behind Jurassic English™
description: The Jurassic English™ framework integrates the Jurassic Thinking Cycle, CEFR progression, and ecocentric pedagogy into a structured school curriculum from Pre-A1 to C1.
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices English EN Tiếng Việt Tiếng Việt Free sample pack Free sample pack Illustration Institutional partner for schools and universities: WorldWise Learning (opens in a new tab) Back to homepage Framework Deep Dive The deeper architecture behind Jurassic English™ This is the detailed view for curriculum leaders, academic reviewers, and institutional decision-makers who need to understand the framework’s research base, instructional standards, ecological extension, governance, and implementation logic. Research-informed and literature-centered Instructionally disciplined and standards-aware Governed for fidelity, scalability, and long-term implementation Core Model Three levels hold the framework together. The guidebook frames Jurassic English™ at three linked levels: what counts as sound judgment, how reasoning is taught, and what teachers and students actually do in the lesson. Epistemological How do we know what is right? Text selection criteria and moral dilemma design Pedagogical How do we teach reasoning? Jurassic Thinking Cycle™, questioning hierarchy, and accountable talk Operational What do teachers and students do? Lesson plan templates, 40/60-minute models, and the rubric system Research Base The framework stands on a clear research spine. The v3.0 guidebook grounds the framework in critical thinking, moral development, disciplinary literacy, cognitive apprenticeship, culturally sustaining pedagogy, language progression, ecocentric education, and Education for Sustainable Development. Critical Thinking The framework embeds elements of thought and intellectual standards directly into questioning, discussion, and written reasoning. Moral Development Ethical reasoning is treated as a staged capability, developed through dilemma analysis and justified judgment. Disciplinary Literacy Literature is used as a disciplinary tool for reasoning rather than as a source of language practice alone. Cognitive Apprenticeship Teacher modelling, scaffolding, and gradual release support students as they move toward independent reasoning. Culturally Sustaining Pedagogy Cultural responsiveness is treated as an intellectual resource that strengthens interpretation, dialogue, and judgment. SLA and CEFR Progression Language progression is planned alongside cognitive demand, including support for sustained development toward the B2 plateau. Ecocentric Education Ecological literacy, place-based text selection, and human-nature relationships become legitimate domains of inquiry. Education for Sustainable Development Critical thinking, systems thinking, and anticipatory thinking extend the framework into ecological and civic responsibility. Evidence in Practice The guidebook’s empirical base translated into classroom relevance Literature-based moral education strengthens character identification, perspective-taking, and ethical interpretation. Structured classroom dialogue improves the quality of reasoning, discussion, and accountable talk. Written justification supports stronger evidence use and more disciplined academic expression. Cross-cultural text analysis deepens interpretation and broadens perspective-taking. Nature-based and eco-themed texts support ecological empathy and environmental awareness. Place-based education improves motivation by grounding learning in local and ecological context. CLIL and content-based instruction strengthen language development through meaningful subject engagement. Instructional Design Standards Access varies. Cognitive challenge does not. The framework combines UDL, differentiation, and self-regulation principles so students can reach the same reasoning architecture through different access pathways. Multiple Means of Engagement Students access meaningful choice in response format and context while staying inside a common reasoning framework. Multiple Means of Representation Texts can be accessed through visual, auditory, and kinesthetic pathways without reducing cognitive demand. Multiple Means of Action and Expression Students show reasoning through essays, debate, artistic response, digital storytelling, and ecological observation. Differentiation Across Language and Reasoning Supports scale from glossaries and sentence frames through to independent inquiry and metacognitive transfer. Regulation-Aware Access Movement, sensory transitions, and attentional resets are treated as conditions that preserve learning access rather than interrupt it. Ecocentric Reasoning Extension Version 3.0 expands the framework without replacing it. Version 3.0 extends the framework through ecocentric reasoning. The living world becomes a legitimate domain of moral and intellectual inquiry rather than a decorative theme. The Jurassic metaphor is used deliberately: language is the fossil record of thought, stories are the strata in which values are preserved, and students become palaeontologists of meaning. At Level 3 and above, teachers are expected to include at least one ecological reflection prompt per unit. What changes in practice Personal reflection connects the text to lived experience. Universal reflection draws out a lesson for the wider human community. Ethical reflection asks what the story means for how we live. Metacognitive reflection tracks how thinking changes. Ecological reflection asks what responsibility the story creates toward the living world. Ecocentric Text Selection Criteria Meaningful human-nature relationships Environmental consequence Stewardship ethic Ecological systems thinking Indigenous ecological knowledge where appropriate Governance and Fidelity The framework is governed, audited, and versioned. The guidebook positions quality assurance as a formal part of implementation, not an optional add-on. Review, moderation, and renewal are built into the model. Termly Lesson Plan Audit A sample of lesson plans is reviewed to confirm fidelity to the framework’s reasoning architecture. Annual Classroom Observation Observed or recorded lessons are reviewed against a shared implementation rubric at higher rollout tiers. Annual Student Portfolio Moderation Cross-classroom moderation calibrates student work against the framework’s reasoning standards. Annual Data Review Programme leaders review placement trends and assessment evidence to identify strengths and gaps. Every 3 years Programme Renewal Curriculum content and research foundations are reviewed formally rather than left to drift. Scalability and Implementation Growth is only valid when fidelity stays intact. The v3.0 guidebook frames expansion as a tiered implementation pathway supported by shared protocols, certification, and quality assurance. Fidelity at Scale The framework treats scale without fidelity as dilution. Growth is only valid if the core intellectual architecture remains intact. Tier 1: Single Classroom Launch A teacher begins by studying the framework, teaching a first lesson, completing one full unit, and submitting reflective evidence. Tier 2: Department or Year-Level Rollout A cohort of teachers shares planning, participates in observation cycles, and calibrates assessment through moderation. Tiered Partnership Model Implementation is supported through certification, shared protocols, and quality assurance infrastructure rather than informal adoption. Next Step Explore implementation with the full framework in view. h1: AI scoring for IELTS Speaking: how to use it well
description: What AI scoring of IELTS Speaking can and cannot tell you, how to use any AI practice well, and when a live human assessment is worth it. Unofficial advice.

Every AI score mentioned here is a practice estimate, not an official IELTS score. English Tiếng Việt Learning resources Key facts An AI score for IELTS Speaking is a practice estimate , not an official IELTS score, and cannot be used for admission, placement or employment. AI is useful for two things: repetition, and pointing to one priority with evidence from your own answers. AI does not replace a live listener for pronunciation or two-way interaction. Typed answers cannot be assessed for pronunciation. Use it well: read the range, not one number; check the evidence; pick one priority; practise on new questions; re-measure. Jurassic AI Speaking is for adults 18+, from 79.000₫ for a Basic report. For a live human assessment: the Live Speaking Baseline, 690.000₫, about 15–20 minutes. "The AI gave me 6.5. Will I get 6.5 in the test?" Nobody knows in advance. What matters is what the number is for. What an AI score is, and is not Only the official test produces an official IELTS score. Everything else is an estimate of which band range today's answers show. Three things follow. AI can only judge what it receives. Typed answers carry no sound, so no pronunciation. A recording adds delivery measures, but it is still a machine measuring a file, not a person listening. One number can mislead. Speaking is rated on four equally weighted criteria, and one mock is a small sample. An honest estimate comes with a range, wider when there is less evidence. Do not compare numbers across tools. Track progress with one tool, one mode (typed with typed) and new questions. What AI does well Repetition: a full three-part mock whenever you want. Evidence: verbatim quotes from your answers instead of "be more fluent". One priority: a well-designed tool picks the change worth making first. What AI cannot do yet Pronunciation needs a listener. The public descriptors frame it around how easily a listener understands you. In Jurassic AI Speaking, speaking mode is a limited beta and its pronunciation figure is a practice estimate from beta measures. Two-way interaction. In Part 3 the person asking reacts to what you just said. A fixed mock trains structure, not that exchange. The cause of a pause. AI can measure where you pause; as our own AI Speaking page says, that does not tell us why. A listener can probe. Your result. No tool or person knows your test score in advance. Six steps to use any AI Speaking practice well Check what the tool received. If typed, ignore any pronunciation conclusion. If spoken, record somewhere quiet with a headset. Read the range, not one number. A 0.5 change between two mocks is usually within normal variation. Track specific indicators instead. Check the evidence. Is the quoted sentence really yours? Is the comment tied to it, or generic advice that fits anyone? Pick one priority. Ask: "If I could fix one thing in the next few weeks, what would lift the most criteria?" Note one strength to keep. Practise structure on new questions; do not memorise rewrites. If a tool rewrites your answer as a "higher band version", read it to see how an idea develops, then practise a sequence of thinking. We use A-R-E : Answer, Reason, Example. It is not a script. Re-measure after two or three weeks , same mode, new questions. No change after two re-measures? Time for a live listener. Also read the privacy notice. With Jurassic AI Speaking, answer text goes to an AI provider outside Vietnam; text and report are deleted automatically after 30 days. Illustrative example From the illustrative sample on our AI Speaking page; not a real learner, not a model to memorise. Suppose you say: "I don't think so… [2.9s pause] because teachers have empathy, you know, and students need human guidance when they are stressed." The longest pause sits between opinion and reason, so the priority is organising that step, not vocabulary. Practise Answer → Reason → Example on unfamiliar questions, then check whether that pause is shorter on new questions. You can ask a teacher to review any report. title: IELTS online test: what a practice test misses in Speaking
h1: IELTS online test: what a practice test can tell you, and what Speaking needs
description: How computer-delivered IELTS differs from an online practice test, what a practice test can mark, why Speaking needs a trained listener, and how to self-check.
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices English EN Tiếng Việt Tiếng Việt Book Baseline · 690k₫ Baseline · 690k₫ Learning resources IELTS online test: what a practice test can tell you, and what Speaking needs Mr. Jay Adams · 14 October 2026 Checked against ielts.org on 14 October 2026. Jurassic English™ is independent and not affiliated with British Council, IDP or Cambridge University Press & Assessment. This is a teacher's advice, not official IELTS guidance. English Tiếng Việt Learning resources Key facts "IELTS online test" can mean the official test on computer at a test centre, IELTS Online taken at home, or an online practice test. Only the first two give you an official IELTS result. In both official computer formats, Speaking is still a conversation with a trained IELTS examiner: face to face at the centre, or by video call for IELTS Online. A practice test can mark Listening and Reading, because each question has one right answer. Speaking is judged on four criteria and needs a trained listener. You can self-check Speaking at home: record yourself, time Part 2 (1 minute to prepare, 1–2 minutes to speak), and listen back for the four criteria. That gives you evidence, not a band. Any practice score, including ours, is not an official IELTS score. Most people who search "ielts online test" want one thing: try a test, see where they stand, before paying for the real one. That is sensible. The trouble is that a practice result can be reliable in one skill and misleading in another, and Speaking is where it misleads most. Official test or practice test The "Ways to take IELTS" page on ielts.org describes two official computer formats: IELTS on computer at a test centre. Listening, Reading and Writing on screen; Speaking face to face with a trained examiner. Results in 1–5 days. IELTS Online at home. Available in some countries, Academic only. Speaking by video call with an examiner. Results in 6–8 days, and each receiving organisation decides whether to accept it. Everything else (official sample materials, apps, centre tests, AI tools) is a practice test, and none of it gives an official result. On 5 March 2026 ielts.org announced that from mid-2026 all IELTS tests move to computer, with timelines varying by market, and that the skills assessed do not change. Computer delivery does not mean talking to a machine: Speaking stays one person talking with another for 11–14 minutes. What a practice test can do: Listening and Reading These skills have right answers, so you can mark yourself. ielts.org publishes official Academic sample tasks for Listening and Reading in the computer interface, each with an answer-key PDF. The site notes the practice experience is not timed, so time yourself. Do each test once, without pausing or replaying, and read your mistakes by type: missed in time, spelling, or misread question. ielts.org also describes the IELTS Trial Test : a familiarisation test with no fee at participating official locations, covering Listening, Reading and Writing, marked by an official examiner, not an official score. The page lists Listening, Reading and Writing only, with no mention of Speaking. What a practice test cannot do: Writing and Speaking Writing and Speaking have no answer key; they are judged against band descriptors. For Speaking, ielts.org's "IELTS scoring in detail" lists four equally weighted criteria: Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Pronunciation. Whether a pause is natural or a search for language, whether an idiom fits or was inserted, whether you are easy or merely possible to follow: these take a trained listener hearing your whole performance. The descriptors themselves say you are rated on average performance across all parts. So treat any online "Speaking band" as an estimate. Ask whether it heard your voice or only read text, whether it shows a range, and whether it points to evidence in your answers. Self-check your Speaking at home Get the tasks. Download the IELTS Speaking sample tasks PDF from ielts.org. Do not prepare answers in advance; if you have already read it, make up new questions of the same type. Record once, like the real test. Part 1: four or five short questions on a familiar topic. Part 2: one minute to prepare with notes, then speak for one to two minutes without stopping. Part 3: three broader questions (an opinion, a comparison, a prediction). No retakes. Listen back four times, one criterion each time. Fluency and Coherence: how long did Part 2 last, and do pauses fall between ideas or mid-sentence before a verb? Lexical Resource: which general words repeat, and can you rephrase when a word is missing? Grammatical Range and Accuracy: which sentence types do you use, and where do errors cluster? Pronunciation: which words could a listener mishear, and do final sounds disappear? Choose one thing to practise. Ask which single change would lift the most criteria. Practise it across many new questions, then record again in two or three weeks and compare the same indicators. Know the limits. You hear what you meant to say. You cannot tell which errors matter most. There are no follow-up questions. And you get evidence, not a band. FAQ Is there an official IELTS online practice test? ielts.org publishes official sample materials: Listening and Reading tasks with answer keys, Writing tasks with example responses, and Speaking sample tasks. You mark them yourself; there is no official score. On computer-delivered IELTS, do I speak to a computer? No. Speaking is face to face with a trained examiner, or by video call for IELTS Online. Can an online practice test give me a Speaking band? Only an estimate, and only useful if it shows evidence from your answers. How long is Speaking Part 2? One minute to prepare, then one to two minutes speaking. The whole Speaking test takes 11–14 minutes. Is a Jurassic AI Speaking score an IELTS score? No. It is a practice estimate with a range. title: IELTS Speaking 6 to 7: Find What Is Holding You Back
h1: IELTS Speaking 6 to 7: what is holding you back
description: How band 6 and band 7 IELTS Speaking differ in the public band descriptors, and how to find the one constraint holding your own answers back. Unofficial advice.
text: Skip to main content Jurassic English ™ Kids Academy (5–12) Ages 9–18 IELTS Writing New AI Speaking Mocks Pricing Products & prices English EN Tiếng Việt Tiếng Việt Book Baseline · 690k₫ Baseline · 690k₫ Learning resources IELTS Speaking 6 to 7: what is holding you back Mr. Jay Adams (CELTA) · 13 October 2026 Checked against the band descriptors on ielts.org on 13 October 2026. Jurassic English™ is independent and not affiliated with British Council, IDP or Cambridge University Press & Assessment. This is a teacher's advice, not official IELTS guidance. English Tiếng Việt Learning resources Key facts The Speaking score comes from four equally weighted criteria: Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, Pronunciation. The gap between band 6 and band 7 is about ease and flexibility : band 6 can speak at length; band 7 speaks at length without visible effort. The four criteria interact: the visible problem is often a symptom. The Jurassic English method: find one primary constraint, show the evidence in your own answers, keep your strengths, practise a structure of thinking rather than memorised answers, then re-measure. No one can promise a band. This guide does not promise 7.0, and Jurassic AI Speaking scores are practice estimates, not official results. Many learners reach me at 6.0 or 6.5 with the same story: lots of vocabulary study, no movement in the score. They are usually fixing several things at once, when the score is held down by one. The four criteria and the public descriptors IELTS publishes its Speaking Band Descriptors on ielts.org. Its "IELTS scoring in detail" page says the four criteria carry equal weight and the Speaking score is their average; rounding rules are explained there. Two notes at the foot of the descriptors matter most. To get a band on a criterion, you must fully fit that band's positive features. And you are rated on your average performance across all parts of the test. That is why "a bit more of everything" rarely moves the score. Band 6 vs band 7, criterion by criterion My paraphrase of the public descriptors, not an official version: Scroll to see more → Criterion Band 6 Band 7 What changes Fluency and Coherence Happy to talk at length, but the thread sometimes breaks when you pause, repeat yourself or restart a sentence. Linking words are there, sometimes in the wrong place. Long turns come "without noticeable effort". You may still pause mid-sentence to find a word, but the listener never loses the thread, and you move between ideas smoothly. Hesitation is still allowed at 7. Losing the thread is not. Lexical Resource You have the words to keep talking about most topics; some choices sound slightly off, yet the meaning gets through, and you can usually say it another way. You adapt your vocabulary to each topic, reach for some less common words and natural word partnerships, and still slip occasionally. Rephrasing works when you need it. Not "harder words" but choosing words to fit the context. Grammatical Range and Accuracy You try complex sentences, but they often carry mistakes, and your choice of structures feels fixed; listeners still understand you. You move between simple and complex sentences without strain; most sentences come out clean, though a few errors, even basic ones, can remain. Clean sentences become the norm. Band 7 still allows errors. Pronunciation Mostly easy to follow, with control that comes and goes: stress and intonation work for a while, then fade, and a few words are unclear. No standalone band 7 descriptor. Band 7 means everything positive at band 6, plus part of what band 8 shows: steady rhythm and flexible intonation over long turns, easy to understand throughout. Keep band 6 stable, then sustain rhythm across longer turns. An ielts.org article (3 December 2025) makes a similar point: at 6 a speaker states opinions; at 7 they build arguments. Why the criteria interact Grammar search breaks fluency. You stop mid-sentence to choose a verb form. It looks like a fluency problem; the root is a structure you know but cannot yet produce automatically. Short ideas make vocabulary look narrow. One claim and one vague reason leave no room for less common words. Memorised phrases hurt coherence. Long openers and inserted idioms sound smooth, then fail to match what follows. Pronunciation is fine, but fluency is the limit. Speech chopped into fragments gives stress and intonation no long sentence to run across. The method: one primary constraint Find one constraint. Ask: "If I could fix only one thing in the next six weeks, what would lift the most criteria?" Show the evidence. Record three Part 3 answers, transcribe them, and mark where each hesitation falls (between ideas, or mid-sentence before a verb), how many real ideas each answer has, and where errors cluster. Keep your strengths. Note what stays the same as well as what changes. Practise structure, not memorised answers. A sequence of thinking (claim, reason, example, consequence) works on any topic. Re-measure. After two or three weeks, record new questions and mark the same indicators. Three illustrative examples Invented to explain the method; not real student answers, not models to memorise. Illustrative example 1: grammar breaking fluency. Asked whether people read less than in the past, suppose you say: "I think... people nowadays, they are... they have... um, they have been reading less, because of the phone... it make people... not focus." Every pause sits just before a verb. The constraint is an unautomated structure, not fluency itself. Say the idea in a structure you control first, then drill the present perfect across many topics. Illustrative example 2: short ideas, narrow vocabulary. Asked how technology has changed work, suppose you say: "Technology makes work easier. People can work at home. It is very convenient." Three sentences, one idea. Develop it: "Many office jobs can now be done remotely, so people skip the daily commute. The downside is that work time and family time get blurred." Remotely , commute and blurred appear because the idea needs them. Illustrative example 3: memorised phrases, lost coherence. Asked whether you enjoy cooking, suppose you say: "Well, that's a really interesting question. In my humble opinion, cooking is a double-edged sword. I don't cook very often because I live with my parents." The idiom matches nothing that follows. Answer directly: "Not really. My mum does most of the cooking, so I only make simple things like fried rice." FAQ What does band 7 in IELTS Speaking require? Ease and flexibility across all four criteria, with some errors and hesitation still allowed. You need to fully fit band 7's positive features on a criterion to get band 7 on it. How long does it take to go from 6.0 to 7.0? No one can answer honestly before hearing you, and practice gains are not a promise about the test. Should I memorise model answers? No. Practise a sequence of thinking instead. Is pronunciation the most important criterion? The four criteria are weighted equally. Check your own evidence before spending months on individual sounds. Is a Jurassic AI Speaking score an IELTS score? No. It is an AI practice estimate with an uncertainty range. Typed answers cannot be assessed for pronunciation. Is Jurassic English linked to British Council, IDP or Cambridge? No. Jurassic English™ is independent, and this advice is unofficial.
